relations.note: Aphrodite frustrates Achilles’ abuse by preserving Hector’s corpse from damage.
Apollo repeatedly opposes Achilles, striking Patroclus and preserving Hector’s corpse.
Apollo helps Paris kill Achilles; some Classical accounts make Apollo effectively the killer.
Athena supports Achilles and deceives Hector during their fatal encounter.
Athena restrains Achilles before he can kill Agamemnon.
Chiron teaches Achilles hunting, medicine, music, and heroic discipline.
Hephaestus makes Achilles’ replacement armor and cosmic shield at Thetis’ request.
Hephaestus checks the attacking river with divine fire.
Hera supports Achilles’ Achaean side and sends Hephaestus against Scamander.
Hermes guides Priam safely into and out of Achilles’ camp.
The Muses lament Achilles during his prolonged funeral observances.
The Nereids join Thetis in lamenting Achilles for seventeen days.
Poseidon intervenes against Achilles’ attack by carrying Aeneas away.
Later tradition says Poseidon creates or grants Leuke for Achilles.
Thetis is Achilles’ divine mother.

relations.myth: Removal from the funeral pyre to Leuke
relations.note: Thetis snatches Achilles from his pyre and conveys him to Leuke.
Achilles is Zeus’ great-grandson through Aegina and Aeacus.

relations.myth: Thetis secures honor through Achaean losses
relations.note: Zeus grants Thetis’ request to honor Achilles by permitting Greek defeats.
Actaeon descends from Aphrodite through Harmonia and Autonoe.
Actaeon is Apollo's grandson through Aristaeus in the standard paternal genealogy.
Actaeon's ghost laments that his divine grandfather Apollo did not save him.
Actaeon descends from Ares through Harmonia and Autonoe.
Actaeon accompanies Artemis in hunting before unwillingly seeing her bath.
Actaeon claims superiority in hunting and incurs Artemis' deadly punishment.
Artemis gives Actaeon deer-form so his dogs kill him.
Artemis punishes Actaeon's erotic spying by transforming him for his hounds.
Diana transforms Actaeon into a stag after he unknowingly enters her grotto.
Athena recounts Actaeon's fate as precedent when explaining Tiresias' lesser punishment.
Chiron creates an image of Actaeon that consoles the grieving dogs.
Chiron rears or trains Actaeon in hunting.
Actaeon's dismemberment foreshadows Dionysus' destruction of their cousin Pentheus.
Actaeon and Dionysus are first cousins through the sisters Autonoe and Semele.
Actaeon is Harmonia's maternal grandson through Autonoe.
Harmonia mourns Actaeon after his destruction.
Zeus becomes angry because Actaeon woos Semele, causing Actaeon's death.

relations.myth: Oracle of the lion and boar
relations.note: Apollo gives the oracle governing the marriages of Adrastus's daughters.
Apollo's response commands Adrastus and Hipponous to cast themselves into fire.

relations.myth: Settlement after recovery of the Argive dead
relations.note: Athena orders an Argive oath binding Adrastus after Theseus recovers the bodies.
Cleisthenes transfers Adrastus's tragic choruses to Dionysus.

relations.myth: Gift of the divine horse Arion
relations.note: Heracles gives Arion to Adrastus; no personal encounter appears in earlier evidence.

relations.myth: Learned derivation of the title Adrasteia
relations.note: Late writers associate Adrasteia's title with Adrastus, without proving original identity.
A Pausanian tradition credits Adrastus with founding a sanctuary of Nemesis.
Zeus sends unfavorable signs, but Adrastus proceeds with the expedition.

relations.myth: Destruction of Adrastus's champions at Thebes
relations.note: Zeus kills Capaneus and opens the earth to preserve Amphiaraus from dishonor.
Apollo sends plague because Agamemnon dishonors Chryses and retains Chryseis.
Artemis frustrates the intended sacrifice by substituting a deer and taking Iphigenia.
Artemis blocks the fleet and demands Iphigenia after Agamemnon kills her deer and boasts.
Athena supports the Achaeans fighting under Agamemnon's command.
Athena prevents Achilles from killing Agamemnon during their quarrel.
Hephaestus makes the divine sceptre that Agamemnon eventually inherits.
Hera supports the Achaean army under Agamemnon's leadership.
Hermes passes the future sceptre of Agamemnon from Zeus to Pelops.
Thetis secures Zeus' action against Agamemnon's army for dishonoring Achilles.
Zeus sends Agamemnon a false dream promising immediate victory.
Agamemnon's inherited sceptre originates with Zeus before passing through the Pelopid dynasty.
Zeus permits Achaean losses against Agamemnon's coalition to vindicate Achilles.
Apollo restores Hector after Ajax knocks him down with a stone.
Apollo helps Paris kill Achilles before Ajax recovers the corpse.
Athena contrives Odysseus’s victory over Ajax in the armor contest.
Athena deludes Ajax into attacking livestock instead of Greek commanders.
Ajax invokes the Erinyes to punish the Atreidae and Greek army.
Heracles prays for Ajax’s birth and interprets Zeus’s eagle omen.
Heracles wraps the infant in lion skin, leaving one vulnerable spot.
Ajax invokes Hermes Chthonios for a swift and painless death.
Poseidon, disguised as Calchas, encourages Ajax and renews his strength.
Thetis sets Achilles’s armor out as the prize disputed by Ajax.
Thetis, Peleus’s wife and Achilles’s mother, is Ajax’s aunt by marriage.
Ajax is Zeus’s great-grandson through Aeacus and Telamon.
Zeus answers Heracles’ prayer by sending an eagle omen.
Zeus grants Ajax light in which to continue fighting.
Apollo protects Admetus because the king treated him piously during servitude.
Apollo yokes a lion and boar, enabling Admetus to win Alcestis.
Apollo serves Admetus as a herdsman after Zeus punishes him.
Artemis fills Admetus’ bridal chamber with snakes after he omits her sacrifice.
Castor and Admetus are co-members of later heroic expedition lists.
Alcestis is received, or is about to be received, among underworld powers.
Admetus conceals Alcestis’ death and hospitably receives Heracles at Pherae.
Plutarch says Heracles’ love for Admetus motivates Alcestis’ recovery.
Heracles overpowers Thanatos and returns the veiled Alcestis to Admetus.
An alternative tradition has Persephone send Alcestis back without Heracles.
Thanatos claims Alcestis when she substitutes herself for Admetus.
Apollo’s oracle resolves the Heracleidae’s dispute by directing that Alcmene be buried at Megara.

relations.myth: Athena stops mad Heracles from killing Amphitryon
relations.note: Athena strikes Heracles unconscious with a stone, saving Amphitryon from his murderous madness.
The birth-goddess prevents Alcmene from delivering until deceived by a female helper.

relations.myth: Hebe and Alcmene share the Cynosarges cult group
relations.note: Hebe receives cult alongside Alcmene, Heracles, and Iolaus without a surviving direct narrative.
Hecate transforms Galinthias and later makes Alcmene’s helper her sacred attendant.

relations.myth: Helios delays sunrise during Zeus’s extended night
relations.note: Zeus orders Helios not to rise while Alcmene is deceived by the divine impersonation.
Hera restrains Alcmene’s delivery so Eurystheus is born first and gains sovereignty.

relations.myth: Hera sends serpents against the infant twins
relations.note: Hera attacks Alcmene’s household by sending two serpents against Heracles and Iphicles.

relations.myth: Amphitryon fights beside Heracles against the Minyans
relations.note: Amphitryon joins Heracles in battle against the Minyans of Orchomenus.
Hera-driven madness turns Heracles against his household, leaving Amphitryon in mortal danger.
Alcmene is Heracles’ biological mother by Zeus.

relations.myth: Heracles returns and saves Amphitryon’s household
relations.note: Heracles returns before Lycus can execute Amphitryon, Megara, and the children.
Amphitryon acts as Heracles’ benevolent instructor and teaches him to drive a chariot.
Mercury impersonates Sosia and helps Jupiter maintain the deception of Alcmene and Amphitryon.

relations.myth: Hermes carries Alcmene to the Blessed Isles
relations.note: At Zeus’s command, Hermes substitutes a stone and transports Alcmene to the Blessed Isles.
Personified Night is associated with the prolonged night surrounding Alcmene’s conception of Heracles.

relations.myth: Poseidon’s golden hair protects Amphitryon’s enemy
relations.note: Poseidon gives Pterelaus the life-preserving hair that structures Amphitryon’s Taphian war.

relations.myth: Selene cooperates in extending Alcmene’s night
relations.note: Some later accounts enlist Selene in the cosmic pause enabling Zeus’s deception.

relations.myth: Zeus impersonates Amphitryon during the extended night
relations.note: Zeus usurps Amphitryon’s identity, reports his victory, and sleeps with Alcmene.

relations.myth: Zeus orders Alcmene removed to the Blessed Isles
relations.note: Later tradition makes Zeus command Alcmene’s bodily removal and substitution with a stone.
Zeus apparently vindicates Alcmene by sending rain against Amphitryon’s attempted burning.

relations.myth: Zeus impersonates Amphitryon and lies with Alcmene
relations.note: Zeus deceives Alcmene by assuming Amphitryon’s appearance and fathers Heracles.
Aphrodite receives worship on another division of Amphiaraus’ Oropian altar.
A late genealogy names Apollo as Amphiaraus’ father.
Apollo loves Amphiaraus and provides his prophetic affiliation.
Amphiaraus adopts Asclepian healing methods and bearded physician iconography without identification.
Amphiaraus frustrates Athena’s plan to immortalize the wounded Tydeus.
Castor hunts beside Amphiaraus and neighbors him on the Tegea pediment.
Harmonia’s necklace passes through Polynices to Eriphyle and determines Amphiaraus’ departure.
Heracles receives worship on another division of Amphiaraus’ great Oropian altar.
Hermes shares a division of the great Oropian altar with Amphiaraus.
Hestia shares a division of the great Oropian altar with Amphiaraus.
The nymphs receive worship on Amphiaraus’ divided altar at Oropos.
Pan receives worship on another division of Amphiaraus’ Oropian altar.
Zeus loves and favors Amphiaraus.
Zeus splits the earth before Periclymenus can strike Amphiaraus.
Aphrodite gave Andromache the marriage veil that falls during her collapse.
Artemis kills Andromache’s ransomed mother in Priam’s house.
Thetis guarantees her marriage to Helenus and the continuation of Molossus’ dynasty.
Andromache seeks divine protection from Hermione’s plot at Thetis’ altar.
Athena places or helps place Andromeda’s image among the stars.
Danaë is Andromeda’s mother-in-law and accompanies the Perseid family.
Andromeda is an ancestress of Heracles through Electryon and Alcmena.
Their separate rescue scenes are juxtaposed as parallel Argive victories.
Medusa’s severed head is used by Perseus against Phineus and his followers.
Offended by Cassiopeia’s comparison, they seek the punishment that places Andromeda in danger.
Poseidon sends flood and monster, indirectly making Andromeda the demanded victim.
They appear as parallel rock-bound prisoners threatened by beasts and rescued by Argive heroes.
Zeus is Andromeda’s divine father-in-law through Perseus.
The chorus compares Antigone's enclosure with Danaë's imprisonment.
They are invoked as supernatural agents of Antigone's family's ruin.
Antigone is poetically presented as a bride proceeding to Hades.
Heracles unsuccessfully petitions Creon to pardon Haemon, indirectly affecting Antigone.
Antigone declares that Creon's burial prohibition did not originate with Zeus.
Virgil alludes to a spider hated by Minerva without naming Arachne.
Aelian contrasts spiders with Athena's weaving gift in a probable Arachne allusion.
Athena raises Arachne and teaches her the art of weaving.
Athena transforms Arachne and Phalanx into crawling creatures after their incest.
Athena transforms Arachne using Hecatean herbs; Hecate does not personally act.
Aphrodite deploys Eros so Medea will assist Jason and the expedition.
Apollo provides light that saves the company from supernatural darkness near Anaphe.
The company sacrifices to Apollo and witnesses his appearance above the sea at Thynias.
The company steals the Fleece guarded within Ares’ Colchian grove and precinct.

relations.myth: Construction and passage through the rocks
relations.note: Athena directs Argo’s construction and pushes the ship through the clashing rocks.
Circe purifies Jason and Medea of blood guilt, then dismisses the company.
Castor sails as the company’s horseman and combatant.
The Boreads pursue the Harpies and force an end to their attacks on Phineus.
Hecate supplies the ritual power Medea invokes to protect Jason during his trials.
The company confronts the fire-breathing bronze bulls made by Hephaestus for Aeëtes.
Hera protects Argo, favors Jason and engineers Medea’s aid and the return.
Heracles joins under Jason, saves the party at Cyzicus and is left searching for Hylas.
Iris stops the Boreads from killing the Harpies and guarantees their oath.
The Nereids pass Argo hand to hand safely through the Planctae.
Polyphemus searches for Hylas and is left behind when Argo departs Mysia.
Scylla threatens Argo, but divine guidance enables the company to avoid her.
The Sirens try to lure the company, but Orpheus overpowers their song.
After Talos blocks the landing, Medea and the company bring about his death.
Thetis leads the Nereids in guiding and carrying Argo through western dangers.
The company, through Euphemus, gives Triton a tripod after receiving his guidance.
Triton guides Argo out of Lake Tritonis and receives the company’s tripod.
Zeus indirectly adjudicates the company’s blood pollution and sends ominous storm signs.
Aphrodite’s apple stratagem causes Atalanta to pause and lose the race.
She supplies Atalanta’s rival with golden apples used to defeat her.
Venus incites Atalanta and Hippomenes to sacrilegious desire after his ingratitude.
Hyginus makes Ares father Parthenopaeus by Atalanta without narrating their encounter.
Atalanta hunts the monstrous boar sent by Artemis against Calydon.
Some late explanations make Artemis transform Atalanta after her broken virginity.
Castor is a named fellow hunter alongside Atalanta.
Zeus transforms Atalanta and Melanion into lions after sanctuary intercourse.
Athena appears in a dream and gives Bellerophon the golden bridle.
Bellerophon kills the fire-breathing, composite monster in Lycia.
Bellerophon is the grandfather of Glaucus through Hippolochus.
Homer names Glaucus as Bellerophon’s mortal father.
Pegasus carries Bellerophon while they kill the Chimera.
Pegasus throws Bellerophon to earth during his attempted heavenly ascent.
Pegasus bears Bellerophon against the Chimera, Amazons, and Solymi.
Poseidon fathers Bellerophon on Eurynome in Glaucus’ household.
Bellerophon sacrifices to Poseidon after receiving Athena’s golden bridle.
Bellerophon seeks the heavenly dwellings and the company of Zeus.
Aphrodite is a wedding participant or gift-giver in later accounts.
As Harmonia’s mother, Aphrodite becomes Cadmus’s divine ancestress by marriage.
Apollo attends and plays at the wedding in expanded accounts.
Apollo directs Cadmus to abandon the search, follow a cow, and found a city.
Hyginus makes Cadmus’s transformation punishment for killing Ares’s dragon.
Ares ultimately rescues Cadmus and Harmonia to the land of the blessed.
Cadmus serves Ares for eight years after killing his sacred offspring.
Cadmus sacrifices the guiding cow to Athena at the foundation site.
Athena grants or validates Cadmus’s rule after his service to Ares.
Athena instructs Cadmus to sow the slain dragon’s teeth.
The Charites sing with the Muses at Cadmus’s wedding.
Cadmus is Dionysus’s maternal grandfather through Semele.
Dionysus prophesies Cadmus’s serpent form, warfare, and eventual rescue.
Cadmus dresses as a Bacchant, dances, and accepts his grandson’s cult.
Her abduction by Zeus launches Cadmus’s unsuccessful wandering and search.
Europa is Cadmus’s sister or close kinswoman in Agenorid traditions.
Harmonia is Cadmus’s wife and the mother of his principal children.
Cadmus and Harmonia marry at a feast attended by the gods.
The spouses lead the Encheleans, defeat Illyrians, and rule together.
Cadmus and Harmonia are jointly transformed into serpents.
Hephaestus makes or gives Harmonia’s necklace in one tradition.
The Muses sing at Cadmus’s divine wedding.
Thetis’s wedding to Peleus is poetically compared with Cadmus’s wedding.
Cadmus assists Zeus’s campaign against Typhon through musical deception.
Disguised as a shepherd, Cadmus distracts Typhon with music for Zeus.
Zeus gives Harmonia to Cadmus as his bride in one account.
Zeus sends the transformed Cadmus and Harmonia to Elysium.
Callisto hunts with Artemis, imitates her clothing, and vows to remain a virgin.
Some modern reconstructions derive Callisto from Artemis Kalliste, but no ancient equation is secure.
Artemis kills bear-shaped Callisto, either through Hera’s prompting or broken-vow anger.
Artemis discovers the pregnancy and expels Callisto from her company.

relations.myth: Artemis transforms Callisto into a bear
relations.note: Hesiodic and Amphis-derived variants make Artemis transform Callisto as punishment.

relations.myth: Hera induces Artemis to shoot Callisto
relations.note: In one variant Hera persuades Artemis to kill the bear-shaped Callisto.

relations.myth: Hera transforms Callisto after Arcas’ birth
relations.note: Jealous Hera transforms Callisto into a bear after she bears Arcas.
Juno petitions Oceanus to prevent Callisto and Arcas from setting into his waters.
At Juno’s request, Tethys prevents catasterized Callisto from entering the sea.
Zeus saves Callisto from death or further danger by placing her among the stars.

relations.myth: Zeus assaults Callisto while disguised as Artemis
relations.note: Zeus assumes Artemis’ or Apollo’s form and rapes or impregnates Callisto.

relations.myth: Zeus conceals Callisto by transforming her
relations.note: One variant makes Zeus transform Callisto into a bear to conceal her.
After receiving prophecy, Cassandra breaks her promise or faith with Apollo.
Apollo makes Cassandra’s truthful prophecies unable to persuade after her refusal.
Apollo’s spit imposes the disabling condition that Cassandra will not be believed.
Apollo desires Cassandra and seeks sexual possession after promising prophetic power.
Apollo teaches Cassandra prophecy in expectation of sexual access.
Cassandra clings to Athena’s image, from which Ajax violently drags her.
Cassandra perceives the avenging powers haunting the House of Atreus.
Cassandra prays to the Sun before entering the palace to die.
Aphrodite afflicts Clytemnestra and her sisters with marital infidelity.
Her ghost condemns Apollo for protecting Orestes while neglecting her blood claim.
Apollo’s oracle authorizes the matricide that brings about Clytemnestra’s death.
Clytemnestra opposes Artemis’ demand for Iphigenia’s sacrifice.
Athena adjudicates the matricide in which Clytemnestra is the absent dead victim.
Castor marched against Agamemnon after Clytemnestra’s coerced marriage.
As deus ex machina, Polydeuces condemns the siblings’ matricide.
Castor is Clytemnestra’s brother and, in Hyginus, shares Tyndareus as father.
Clytemnestra’s ghost rouses them and commissions their pursuit of Orestes.
Clytemnestra says she formerly honoured the Erinyes with nocturnal offerings.
Clytemnestra prays to Zeus Teleios while preparing her design against Agamemnon.
Daedalus constructs a sanctuary support and golden ram for Aphrodite.
Daedalus makes Apollo's temple doors depicting the Cretan story.
Daedalus dedicates his wings to Apollo after reaching Cumae.
Daedalus constructs a dancing place for Ariadne at Knossos.
Daedalus advises Ariadne to give Theseus the guiding thread.
Homer compares Hephaestus's divine craftsmanship with Daedalus's human work at Knossos.
Daedalus dedicates a wooden image of Heracles in thanks for an unspecified benefit.
Heracles recognizes and buries Daedalus's drowned son in the sail variant.
A comic wooden Hermes claims Daedalus made him able to speak and walk.
Daedalus's artificial cow enables Pasiphae to conceive the Minotaur.
Daedalus builds the labyrinth that conceals and confines the Minotaur.
Pasiphae supplies Daedalus with a ship or conceals him from Minos.
Daedalus constructs the cow-shaped apparatus enabling Pasiphae's union with the bull.
Poseidon's punishment creates the crisis for which Daedalus constructs Pasiphae's cow.
Daedalus kills his inventive pupil and nephew out of jealousy.
Aphrodite poetically presides as umpire over the bridal struggle.
Artemis transforms Meleager’s mourning sisters; Deianira is spared or subsequently restored.
Athena appears beside Deianira in some vase scenes of the Achelous contest.
A variant genealogy names Dionysus rather than Oeneus as her father.
Dionysus intervenes so Deianira and Gorge are spared or restored.
Hebe becomes Heracles’ divine wife after Deianira has died.
Deianira contrasts Hera’s glorious persecution of Hercules with Venus’ humiliating power.
Heracles wins Deianira’s hand and becomes her husband.
Deianira unwittingly sends the garment whose poison causes Heracles’ mortal death.
Heracles shoots Nessus while the centaur assaults or abducts Deianira.
In the confused variant, Heracles rescues the woman called Deianira from Eurytion.
Hyginus says Heracles seduced or impregnated an alternate Deianira after promising marriage.
Hermes appears beside Deianira in some vase scenes of the Achelous contest.
Deianira’s garment takes effect while Heracles sacrifices to his father Zeus.
Pyrrha is the daughter of Epimetheus in the canonical genealogy.
Deucalion identifies Earth's stones as the Great Mother's bones in Themis's oracle.
The Syrian Deucalion builds a temple and altars in Atargatis's sanctuary landscape.
Hermes communicates Zeus's offered wish, prompting Deucalion to request people.
Deucalion is repeatedly named as Prometheus's son.

relations.myth: Prometheus warns Deucalion before the flood
relations.note: Prometheus warns Deucalion and directs him to provision and build a chest.

relations.myth: Oracle of the Great Mother's bones
relations.note: Themis instructs the couple cryptically to cast their mother's bones behind them.
Triton blows his conch to recall the waters after Jupiter ends the flood.
Zeus orders the stone procedure that allows the couple to restore humanity.

relations.myth: Jupiter commands the throwing of stones
relations.note: Jupiter directly commands Deucalion and Pyrrha to throw stones.
After Deucalion sacrifices, Zeus offers him a wish through Hermes.
Zeus sends the flood against the Bronze race; the couple survives.
Jupiter destroys humanity but preserves the righteous and pious couple.

relations.myth: Parnassian descent and settlement at Opus
relations.note: The couple descends from Parnassus and settles by Zeus's ordinance.
Deucalion sacrifices to Zeus Phyxios after leaving the chest.
Diomedes wounds Aphrodite’s hand while she carries Aeneas from battle.
Aphrodite avenges her wound by corrupting Aegialeia against Diomedes.
Aphrodite punishes Diomedes indirectly by transforming his companions into birds.
Diomedes advances three times against Apollo before the god repels and warns him.
Diomedes wounds Ares with Athena’s concealment, protection, and decisive assistance.
Athena conceals herself, deflects Ares’ spear, and drives Diomedes’ attack.
Athena sends an omen and guides Diomedes and Odysseus during their raid.
Athena grants Diomedes strength, radiance, divine sight, and permission to wound Aphrodite.
Athena heals Diomedes after Pandarus wounds him.
Athena guides Diomedes safely home from Troy in the Homeric return.
Athena makes Diomedes an immortal god.
Diomedes and Glaucus refuse combat after recognizing inherited guest-friendship.
Diomedes exchanges bronze armor for Glaucus’ far more valuable gold armor.
Hephaestus saves Idaeus after Diomedes kills Idaeus’ brother Phegeus.
Hera supports the Achaean side during Diomedes’ greatest battlefield successes.
Aphrodite and Ares complain to Zeus after Diomedes wounds them.
Zeus removes Glaucus’ judgment during his unequal exchange with Diomedes.

relations.myth: Divine settlement after the palace siege
relations.note: Apollo settles Electra’s fate and commands her marriage to Pylades.
Electra supports the revenge commanded by Apollo’s oracle and prays to him.
Electra invokes Ares chiefly as a divine image of murderous violence.
Electra’s attempted attack upon Iphigenia occurs at Artemis’s altar.
Castor condemns the siblings’ agency in matricide and prescribes their futures.
Castor orders Electra to leave and marry Pylades after the matricide.
Castor includes Polydeuces when speaking of the Dioscuri, without a separate exchange.
Electra invokes avenging powers, although they principally pursue Orestes rather than her.
Electra and Orestes ask Earth to send up or empower their father’s spirit.

relations.myth: Lament to the house of Hades
relations.note: Electra addresses the house of Hades during her mourning for Agamemnon.
Electra joins invocations asking underworld Hermes to guide or support the avengers.
Electra prays to Persephone for victory while performing rites at Agamemnon’s tomb.
Electra invokes Zeus as guarantor of justice without receiving a personal epiphany.
Aphrodite keeps dogs from Hector's corpse and anoints it with ambrosial oil.
Apollo repeatedly protects and assists Hector during the Trojan fighting.
Apollo strikes and disorients Patroclus before Hector delivers the fatal wound.
Apollo shields Hector's corpse with the aegis during Achilles' repeated dragging.
Ares supports the Trojans while Hector rallies their forces under his favor.
Athena takes Deiphobus' shape and induces Hector to stand against Achilles.
Athena supports Greek champions and frustrates Hector's attacks.
Glaucus reproaches Hector and joins him in fighting over Sarpedon's body.
Hera opposes Troy and rejects Zeus' impulse to save Hector.
Hermes guides and conceals Priam during the mission to recover Hector's corpse.
Iris carries Zeus' instructions to Priam concerning recovery of Hector's body.
Poseidon secretly strengthens the Achaeans against Hector's assault.
Thetis communicates Zeus' command that Achilles release Hector's corpse.
Zeus grants Hector temporary military success and encourages him with thunder.
The systematized Trojan genealogy makes Hector a descendant of Zeus through Dardanus.
Zeus weighs Hector's fate against Achilles' and permits Hector's allotted death.
Hecuba accuses Helen of disguising personal desire as Aphrodite's compulsion.
A minority genealogy makes Apollo father Hector by Hecuba.
In Stesichorus's variant, Apollo carries Hecuba to Lycia.
Hecuba selects Athena's robe and convenes the women, but Athena refuses their prayer.
Later interpretation links Hecuba with Hecate through their names, dogs, and Thracian setting.
Lycophron makes transformed Hecuba a terrifying canine attendant of Hecate.
Hecuba prepares wine for Priam's prayer and libation to Zeus.
Aphrodite leads Helen astray from husband, child, and parents.
Aphrodite threatens Helen and compels her to return to Paris’s bed.
Apollo snatches Helen away from Orestes and Pylades.
Apollo makes Helen immortal and orders her worship as sailors’ protector.
The Dioscuri secure Helen’s escape and announce her future maritime divinity.
Castor invades Attica with Polydeuces and recovers Helen from Theseus.
The Dioscuri invade Attica and recover Helen from Theseus.
Castor is Helen’s brother, with mortal or divine allocation varying.
Hera creates Helen’s cloud-image while the real Helen is taken to Egypt.
Hermes conveys the real Helen to Proteus’s Egypt for safekeeping.
Nemesis bears Helen after Zeus pursues and impregnates her.
Proteus detains and protects Helen from Paris until Menelaus retrieves her.
Zeus is Helen’s divine father in the principal genealogical tradition.
Apollo confronts Heracles over the capture of Artemis’ sacred hind.
Heracles fights Apollo after seizing the tripod when refused an oracle.
Apollo’s Delphic oracle directs Heracles toward purification and Eurystheus’ service.
Ares fights Heracles while defending his son Cycnus.
Artemis confronts Heracles for capturing her sacred hind.
Athena repeatedly protects and assists Heracles during his exploits.
Athena gives Heracles bronze rattles for driving out the birds.
Athena strikes Heracles unconscious, preventing him from killing Amphitryon.
Heracles tricks Atlas into resuming the burden of the sky.
Heracles holds the sky while Atlas retrieves the apples.
Heracles subdues Cerberus unarmed, displays him, then returns him to Hades.
Heracles accidentally wounds Chiron with a Hydra-poisoned arrow.
Dionysus and Heracles fight together in Gigantomachy traditions.
At Hera’s order, Eileithyia delays Alcmene’s delivery of Heracles.
Heracles drives the boar through snow and captures it alive.
Heracles kills the triple-bodied cattle owner and takes his herd.
Heracles wounds Hades during an otherwise incompletely preserved conflict.
Hades permits Heracles to take Cerberus if he uses no weapons.
Heracles marries the divine personification of youth on Olympus.
Heracles threatens Helios with his bow during the western journey.
Helios lends Heracles his golden cup for crossing Ocean.
Hephaestus makes the bronze clappers Athena provides to Heracles.
Heracles wounds Hera during their prolonged divine hostility.
Hera delays Heracles’ birth and secures Eurystheus’ precedence.
Hera sends two snakes, which the infant Heracles strangles.
Hera causes or commands the madness in which Heracles kills his family.
Heracles and Hera are reconciled when he joins the Olympians.
Hermes assists, conducts or equips Heracles in labour and Underworld traditions.
Iris commands Lyssa to inflict madness upon Heracles for Hera.
In one version Heracles kills Ladon and takes the golden apples.
Heracles destroys the many-headed Hydra and poisons his arrows with its bile.
Heracles strangles or clubs the invulnerable lion and takes its hide.
Heracles wrestles and restrains Nereus to obtain directions.
Nike appears with Heracles in cultic and victorious imagery.
Heracles kills Geryon’s two-headed guard dog.
Pan occasionally appears beside Heracles in regional cult and art.
Persephone receives Heracles and intervenes in Underworld traditions.
Polyphemus joins Heracles in searching Mysia for the abducted Hylas.
Poseidon opposes Heracles during the Pylian campaign.
Heracles frees Prometheus by killing the eagle that torments him.
Prometheus directs Heracles toward Atlas and the Hesperides.
Heracles frightens the birds into flight and shoots them.
Heracles wrestles and defeats Death to restore Alcestis.
Themis participates in divine knowledge concerning Heracles’ apotheosis.
Heracles wrestles Triton in prominent Archaic visual representations.
Zeus is Heracles’ biological father through union with Alcmene.
Zeus admits Heracles to Olympus after his mortal death.
Zeus rescues Heracles from the storm sent by Hera.
She punishes his refusal of her honors by making Phaedra desire him.
Troezenian tradition credited Hippolytus with founding Artemis Lykeia’s local temple.
Artemis reveals his innocence, reconciles him with Theseus and promises lasting cult.
He hunts in Artemis’ company, praises her chastity and offers her a garland.
An Epidaurian stele reportedly recorded his dedication of twenty horses to Asclepius.
The divine healer reassembles or revives Hippolytus after his fatal chariot wreck.
Poseidon’s bull terrifies the horses, causing Hippolytus’ fatal chariot wreck.
Apollo indirectly commands Inachus to expel Io under threat from Zeus.
Argus confines and watches Io until Hermes kills him.

relations.myth: Hera claims Io and sends the gadfly
relations.note: Hera confines Io under Argus and drives her wandering with a gadfly.
Io serves as Hera’s priestess or cult-attendant at Argos.
Some later summaries make Hera, rather than Zeus, transform Io.
Heracles is Io’s remote descendant, prophesied to free Prometheus.

relations.myth: Hermes kills Argus and releases Io
relations.note: Zeus sends Hermes to free Io by killing her vigilant guard.

relations.myth: Prometheus foretells Io’s route and descendants
relations.note: The bound Titan explains Io’s suffering and reveals her future wanderings and lineage.
Zeus is Io’s divine partner and father of Epaphus.

relations.myth: Io regains human form in Egypt
relations.note: Zeus secures or performs Io’s restoration after her wanderings.

relations.myth: Zeus pursues and sexually coerces Io
relations.note: Zeus desires Io; accounts describe seduction, coercion, or rape.

relations.myth: Io is changed into a heifer
relations.note: Zeus transforms Io into a cow to conceal their encounter.

relations.myth: Orestes sent to recover the Taurian image
relations.note: Apollo’s oracle sends Orestes to Tauris, indirectly causing their reunion and escape.
The cult title Artemis Iphigeneia associates or compounds Iphigenia with Artemis.
Roman tradition equates Iphigenia with Diana in the Arician cult complex.
Artemis halts the fleet and requires Iphigenia because of Agamemnon’s offense or vow.
Artemis snatches Iphigenia away and replaces her with a deer.
Artemis transports her to the Tauri and appoints her priestess.
Artemis immortalizes Iphigenia after substituting an animal or phantom.
Athena commands Thoas to release Iphigenia, Orestes, and their companions.
Athena assigns Iphigenia to serve Artemis at Brauron and foretells her burial.
Iphigenia becomes Hecate by Artemis’s will in Hesiodic and Stesichorean testimony.
Through Lapithes, Diodorus’s genealogy gives Ixion remote descent from Apollo.

Athena carries Ixion’s punitive wheel in the Attic kantharos scene.

relations.note: In later accounts Hera reports Ixion’s advance and helps expose his offense.

relations.note: Ixion illicitly approaches or attempts to rape Hera while enjoying Zeus’s favor.
Hermes restrains or binds Ixion to the wheel at Zeus’s command.

relations.myth: Orpheus performs before the underworld rulers
relations.note: She is present as underworld queen when Orpheus’s performance halts Ixion’s punishment.
Zeus fashions a cloud resembling Hera to expose Ixion’s illicit desire.
Zeus imposes Ixion’s endless punishment for ingratitude and his offense against Hera.
Zeus receives the polluted suppliant, purifies him, and admits him to divine favor.
Aphrodite gives Jason the iynx spell that inflames Medea’s desire.
Jason sacrifices to Apollo Embasios before the Argo sails.
Jason dedicates an image or shrine to Artemis during the return voyage.

relations.myth: Building and voyage of the Argo
relations.note: Athena directs the Argo’s construction and helps Jason’s ship through the Symplegades.
Athena attends Jason as the serpent disgorges him in a unique vase image.
Chiron raises Jason and gives him his name.
Circe purifies Jason and Medea from the pollution of Apsyrtus’s killing.
Castor sails as a companion under Jason’s command.
Jason performs Medea’s prescribed nocturnal rite to Hecate before using the drug.
Hera saves the Argo because Jason is dear to her.
Jason carries the disguised Hera across the river and loses one sandal.
Heracles refuses command in Jason’s favor and joins his expedition.
Heracles rebukes Jason and the crew for lingering with the Lemnian women.
Talos opposes Jason’s returning ship and is destroyed by Medea.
The Libyan god assists Jason and the stranded Argonauts and gives guidance or a clod.
Apollo sends serpents after Laocoön violates his prohibition against marriage and procreation.
Laocoön and his children are killed after his sexual sacrilege before Apollo’s image.
Apollo sends two serpents as a sign; they kill Laocoön’s sons but not him.
Laocoön serves Apollo as his priest in Hyginus and Servius.
Artemis appears beside Apollo while Laocoön’s household suffers the serpent attack.
Athena blinds Laocoön and summons serpents that kill his sons.
The serpents shelter beneath Minerva’s image, prompting belief that Laocoön was divinely punished.
Laocoön is chosen as Neptune’s priest and sacrifices a bull when attacked.
Sophocles’ fragment places an invocation of Poseidon within Laocoön’s story.
Leda bears Castor to Tyndareus.

relations.myth: Leda is deified under Nemesis’s name
relations.note: A late Christian account claims Leda became Nemesis after death.

relations.myth: Nemesis lays Helen’s egg for Leda to foster
relations.note: Nemesis bears Helen’s egg, which is delivered to Leda for custody.
Some traditions place Phoebe among Leda’s daughters or Tyndarid family.

relations.myth: Zeus approaches Leda disguised as a swan
relations.note: Zeus assumes a swan’s form and gains sexual access through deception.
At Hera and Athena's request, Aphrodite persuades Eros to inflame Medea.
Aphrodite teaches Jason the charm that secures Medea's assistance.
Apollo reveals Anaphe and saves the voyagers; Medea joins the resulting rites.
Athena joins Hera in seeking Aphrodite's help to manipulate Medea.
Circe is Medea's aunt in the Hesiodic solar genealogy.
Circe purifies Medea and Jason of blood guilt, then rebukes and expels them.
Dionysus asks Medea to restore his nurses to youth.
Diodorus rationalizes Hecate as Medea's mortal mother by Aeëtes.
Medea invokes or serves Hecate in Hellenistic and Roman accounts.
Medea is Helios's granddaughter through Aeëtes.
Helios supplies his granddaughter with the chariot used to escape Corinth.
Hera engineers Medea's passion so her aid to Jason will destroy Pelias.
Medea uses Hera's sanctuary for her children and establishes their rites.
In one variant Medea offers immortality, then removes Talos's vein nail.
Medea destroys Crete's bronze guardian through hostile visions and enchantment.
Themis communicates Zeus's purification command to Hera; Medea receives it indirectly.
Thetis helps the Argo under Hera's orders while Medea is aboard.
Zeus requires Medea and Jason to undergo purification for Apsyrtus's murder.
Apollo supports the Curetes and kills Meleager with arrows in an early variant.
Later mythographers make Ares Meleager's biological father.
The Hesiodic Catalogue calls Meleager loved of Ares.
Artemis sends the boar whose death and trophies bring catastrophe upon Meleager's family.
Castor hunts beside Meleager in early iconography.
Castor and Meleager sail together as Argonauts.
The night-wandering Erinys hears Althaea's curse against Meleager.
Althaea invokes Hades to bring death upon Meleager.
Heracles aims at Meleager's shade, then listens to him and weeps.
Heracles and the youthful Meleager belong to the Argonautic crew.
Althaea invokes Persephone to bring death upon Meleager.
Eos is Memnon’s immortal mother.
Eos petitions Zeus and obtains immortality for Memnon.

relations.myth: Recovery and mourning after Memnon’s death
relations.note: Eos recovers or mourns Memnon’s body after Achilles kills him.
The rising Sun awakens Memnon’s statue, whose voice salutes Eos.

Their divine mothers plead on opposing sides while the heroes’ fates are weighed.
Zeus grants Eos’ request that Memnon receive immortality.
In Ovid, Jupiter grants commemorative birds in response to Aurora’s grief.
Zeus weighs the destinies of Memnon and Achilles before their duel.
Aphrodite frustrates Menelaus’ victory by removing Paris from his grip.
Aphrodite restrains Menelaus’ anger and prevents him from killing Helen.
Menelaus is sacrificed to Artemis through Iphigenia in a late variant.

Through marriage to Zeus’ daughter Helen, Menelaus is Zeus’ son-in-law.
Zeus oversees Menelaus’ duel with Paris and the subsequent broken treaty.
Midas reportedly dedicates his royal judgment-throne at Apollo's Delphi.

Apollo gives Midas ass's ears for rejecting the musical verdict.
Dionysus grants Midas the disastrous power to turn touched objects gold.
Dionysus instructs Midas how to relinquish the golden touch.
Midas hosts Silenus and returns him to Dionysus.
Hermes leads or restrains bound Silenus before the enthroned Midas.
An uncertain Iris or Eileithyia-like goddess appears behind Midas.
After renouncing wealth, Midas follows Pan in the countryside.
Midas alone rejects Tmolus' verdict and prefers Pan's pipes.
Hyginus names Pan as an alternate opponent of Apollo.
Zeus' sanctuary at Ancyra reportedly preserved the anchor found by Midas.
Amphitrite supports Theseus and gives him gifts, enabling him to defeat Minos’s test.

Minos guards or confines Ariadne before she aids Theseus and flees Crete.
Europa bears Minos to Zeus.

Pasiphae is Minos’s wife and mother of his principal children.
Poseidon sends Minos a magnificent bull after Minos prays for a divine sign.

Minos rejects Scylla and, in some versions, ties her to his ship or has her drowned.
Scylla falls in love with Minos and betrays her father and city for him.
Zeus is Minos’s divine father.

relations.myth: Ring challenge aboard the tribute ship
relations.note: Zeus answers Minos’s invocation with lightning during his contest with Theseus.
Minos periodically consults Zeus and derives his laws from the god.

Earth conceals Echo's scattered limbs after her dismemberment.
Juno restricts Echo to repeating others' concluding words.
Hermes points out Narcissus among the beautiful dead.
The Muses preserve Echo's imitative voice after her bodily destruction.
The Muses teach Echo music.
Nemesis makes Narcissus love an image he cannot possess.
Pan repeatedly pursues Echo, but she successfully evades him.
Pan drives pastoral people mad, causing them to dismember Echo.
Pan embraces Echo and teaches her to reproduce songs.
Selene is Narcissus' mother in the Latmian genealogy.
Neoptolemus challenges Apollo over Achilles’ death or attacks his sanctuary.
Apollo’s hostility brings Neoptolemus to a fatal end at Delphi.
After death Neoptolemus remains in Apollo’s precinct overseeing heroic rites.
Neoptolemus joins the horse operation conducted under Athena’s protection.

relations.note: Heracles’ epiphany commands Neoptolemus and Philoctetes to sail to Troy.
Thetis is Neoptolemus’ divine grandmother through Achilles.
Thetis warns Neoptolemus to return from Troy overland.
The Aeacid genealogy makes Neoptolemus a descendant of Zeus.
Neoptolemus kills Priam at Zeus Herkeios’ household altar.

Zeus turns the people to stone, leaving Niobe's children unburied nine days.
Zeus grants Niobe's prayer to be transformed into stone.
Aeolus hosts Odysseus and gives him the winds in a bag.
Odysseus invokes Apollo before beginning the suitors' slaughter.
Ares supports the Brygians against Odysseus until Athena intervenes.

Athena stops renewed civil violence and secures peace on Ithaca.
Athena disguises Odysseus as an old beggar and later restores him.
Calypso compulsorily keeps Odysseus seven years and offers immortality.

Heracles appears and commands the resolution opposed by Odysseus' earlier scheme.
Odysseus encounters the image or shade of Heracles among the dead.

Odysseus calls himself Nobody and escapes beneath Polyphemus' sheep.
Odysseus blinds Polyphemus after the Cyclops eats six crewmen.
After Odysseus reveals his name, Polyphemus invokes Poseidon's vengeance.
Odysseus must travel inland and sacrifice to reconcile with Poseidon.
Poseidon obstructs Odysseus' return and wrecks his raft.
Odysseus arms himself but cannot prevent Scylla killing six companions.
Odysseus twice evades Charybdis' destructive whirlpool.
Odysseus hears their promised knowledge while bound safely to the mast.
Zeus permits Athena's aid and sanctions peace after the suitors' deaths.
Zeus destroys Odysseus' ship after the crew slaughters Helios' cattle.

relations.myth: Oracles of patricide, incest, and pollution
relations.note: Apollo predicts Oedipus’s crimes and commands investigation of Laius’s unpunished murder.
Oedipus invokes Athena’s city and territory without meeting her personally.
Oedipus’s rejected corpse is secretly buried within Demeter’s precinct.

relations.note: Oedipus enters their grove, prays to them, and gains his destined resting place.

Oedipus speaks of entering Hades, but no direct meeting is narrated.
Oedipus’s promised grave enters the Colonus landscape sacred to Poseidon.
Oedipus defeats the Sphinx by answering her riddle; she then destroys herself.

Apollo purifies Orestes, directs his flight, and defends him at trial.
Apollo ends the crisis and assigns Orestes’ trial and marriage.
Orestes obeys Apollo’s command to kill his father’s murderers.

Their black forms afflict Orestes until his finger sacrifice brings recovery.

Hermes warns Aegisthus that Orestes will avenge Agamemnon.
Orestes invokes Zeus in pursuing vengeance for Agamemnon.
Aphrodite rescues Butes after Orpheus’s counter-song fails to retain him.

Orpheus abandons Dionysus and worships Apollo as the greatest god.
Orpheus pacifies the underworld guardian with his music.

Chiron advises Jason to include Orpheus in the Argonautic expedition.
Pseudepigrapha present Orpheus as authoritative revealer of Demeter’s wanderings and rites.
Dionysus sends Dionysiac women to dismember Orpheus after his devotion to Apollo.
Bacchus avenges Orpheus by turning the Ciconian murderers into trees.
Orpheus teaches or performs initiatory rites associated with Dionysus.
Castor is Orpheus’s fellow Argonaut and participates in Orpheus-led rites or songs.

Orpheus charms and petitions Hades, who conditionally releases his wife.

Orpheus greets Helios at dawn, worshipping the sun as Apollo.
Heracles and Orpheus serve together among the Argonauts.
Hermes escorts or reclaims Eurydice as Orpheus loses her again.

The Muses patronize Orpheus, mourn him, gather his remains, and bury him.
Orpheus moves Persephone with song, and she participates in releasing his wife.

Poseidon and the Fates execute vengeance for Palamedes through the Greek fleet’s destruction.

Hyginus says Minerva gives life to the clay figure made by Vulcan.

Hephaestus forms Pandora from earth and water, giving her voice and strength.

relations.note: Zeus designs Pandora as a destructive gift whose arrival permanently changes human life.
Aphrodite promises Paris marriage with Helen and encourages his expedition.

Apollo and Paris jointly kill Achilles near the Scaean gates.

Paris rejects Athena's claim and offer in favor of Aphrodite.

Hermes conducts the three goddesses to Paris on Zeus's order.

relations.note: Themis helps Zeus plan the war sequence in which Paris becomes instrumental.
Thetis's wedding provides the setting for the quarrel Paris later judges.

relations.myth: Apollo incites Hector disguised as Asius

Zeus grants only part of Achilles’ prayer and ordains Patroclus’ death sequence.

Aphrodite attends Peleus’ wedding and ultimately wins the resulting judgment of Paris.
Apollo attends and sings at the wedding of Peleus and Thetis.

The Nereids flee or witness Peleus’ violent seizure of their sister Thetis.
